subject: Post-demo: candidate models + streaming UX notes and next actions
messages:
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Liu <emma@heliocare.com>, Samir Patel <samir.patel@heliocare.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 15 Sep 2026 17:14:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: candidate models + streaming UX notes and next actions

Hi Emma / Samir —

Thanks again for taking the demo this morning. Quick recap and my proposed next steps so we can move to a short eval run: 

Summary of fit (from today's call)
- Primary use case: real-time patient triage chat embedded in HelioCare's portal (short, multi-turn dialogs, frequent interruptions).
- Latency requirement: 90th pct under 300ms for partial streaming tokens; end-of-answer time ideally < 800ms for 90th pct.
- Quality: high factual consistency for triage recommendations and strict stop behavior when clinician phrases like "end session" or specific code tokens are present.

Model recommendations for initial eval (balanced cost / latency for streaming):
1) redwood-turbo-m3-3b (intended: low-latency streaming, good instruction following) — recommended baseline for throughput testing.
2) open-gpt-q5-6b (quantized variant) — to validate cost savings with slightly degraded long-form coherence; useful as fallback for non-critical flows.
3) redwood-guard-8b (higher quality) — evaluate for worst-case fallback when triage answer must include diagnosis-critical language.

Benchmarks & artifacts I linked:
- Shared benchmark sheet: https://drive.redwood/HelioCare/evals/DEAL-7421 (tab: streaming-latency)
- Prompt set (v1) attached as prompt-set-v1.md — includes stop-token tests and clinician-phrases to validate.
- Proposed evaluation plan attached: 20260915-helio-eval-plan.xlsx (3-day run, 2k sessions, both streaming and non-streaming endpoints).

Streaming UX / quality concerns observed in demo (what we should validate):
- Partial output incoherence: when the user interrupts mid-response we saw truncated sentences and disconnected followups. Need to test prefix-preservation and token continuity across interrupt/continue flows.
- Stop-sequence sensitivity: custom clinician phrases must reliably terminate generation. We'll include aggressive stop token tests and negative examples.
- Latency vs. chunk-size tradeoff: we should test small minimal-chunk outputs (1-2 tokens) vs grouped streaming (8-12 tokens) to find the sweet spot for HelioCare's UX.

Proposed immediate next steps (week 1)
1) Run 3-day eval using the attached plan (we'll provision a short Dedicated pool for consistent latency).
2) You send 50 sample triage dialogs (redacted) by EOD Friday; we will synthesize the rest to reach 2k sessions.
3) Rafael to run initial streaming/stop-token tests and share latency + coherence artifacts.
4) Quick 30-min sync next Wed to review results and pick the production model.

A couple of asks for you:
- Please confirm whether PHI will be included in the eval data (will change logging/KMS needs).
- If HelioCare legal needs an NDA before we provision dedicated capacity, flag now.

I put Rafael and Marissa on cc for engineering/evangelism follow-up.

Thanks —
Olga Petrov
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
olga.petrov@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0173

Subject: Re: Post-demo: candidate models + streaming UX notes and next actions

Emma / team —

Thanks for the log, Emma — that's helpful. A few quick engineering notes after a fast pass: 

- Dedicated pool + streaming: yes, Dedicated supports streaming with KV-cache persistence for typical session lengths (we need to size the pool correctly). I'll include a config suggestion in the eval plan.
- Stop tokens: we added "/done" and "#stop" to prompt-set-v1.md and extended the negative examples. We've also baked in multi-token stop checks and an aggressive backoff.
- Truncated output: the demo-log shows an interrupt while the model emitted a multi-part clause. Two mitigations we've proposed in the plan:
  * Prefix-hold: on interrupt, persist the in-flight prefix and continue generation from the last stable token (reduces disjointed tails).
  * Micro-chunking: reduce chunk size to 4 tokens for high-interruption flows; tradeoff is a small latency bump but better coherence.

Action items I own:
- Run a 4-model micro-benchmark overnight (redwood-turbo-m3-3b, open-gpt-q5-6b, redwood-guard-8b, and redwood-mini-1b) focused on 90th pct streaming latency and stop token recall. Expect results by EOD tomorrow (Thu).
- Upload raw latency traces + a short artifact (coherence_samples_v1.json) to the shared Drive.

Olga — once we get the sample dialogs, I'll map them to the prompt-set and kick off the Dedicated run.

Rafael
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
